metrics.extracellular_face: N-terminus + 3 Extracellular Loops (ECL1–3) forming the ligand-binding pocket
metrics.intracellular_face: C-terminus + 3 Intracellular Loops (ICL1–3) interacting with heterotrimeric G proteins

mechanism: GPCRs (the largest family of cell surface receptors in eukaryotes) perceive diverse extracellular stimuli—ranging from photons (rhodopsin), odorants, and ions to hormones, neurotransmitters, and large peptide growth factors.

Upon agonist binding, conformational changes ripple through the transmembrane helices (specifically shifting TM6 outward), creating an intracellular binding cavity that accommodates the alpha-subunit of a cognate heterotrimeric G protein.
csir_high_yield: Rhodopsin Structural Paradigm: In bovine rhodopsin (the prototype GPCR structure solved by X-ray crystallography), 11-cis-retinal is covalently attached via a Schiff base to a conserved Lysine residue in TM7.
Family Classification (GRAFS system): GPCRs are grouped into Glutamate, Rhodopsin (Class A, largest), Adhesion, Frizzled/Taste2, and Secretin families.
pathology: Familial Calcium-Sensing Receptor Mutations: Activating mutations in the GPCR calcium-sensing receptor cause autosomal dominant hypocalcemia, whereas inactivating mutations cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.
lab_workbench: Radioligand Binding Assay (Scatchard Plot Analysis): Uses tritium-labeled agonists or antagonists (3H-ligand) to determine receptor density (Bmax) and dissociation constant (Kd) in cellular membrane preparations.

node_rtk_architecture.title: Receptor Tyrosine Kinases (RTKs)
node_rtk_architecture.subtitle: Single-Pass Transmembrane Catalytic Receptors (EGFR, PDGFR, InsR)

metrics.membrane_topology: Single hydrophobic transmembrane alpha-helix connecting extracellular ligand-binding domain to intracellular tyrosine kinase domain
metrics.activation_mechanism: Ligand-induced Dimerization or Oligomerization followed by trans-autophosphorylation

mechanism: RTKs mediate responses to growth factors, cytokines, and hormones regulating cell proliferation, differentiation, and survival.

Binding of a divalent or dimeric ligand (e.g., EGF) induces receptor dimerization. This brings the intracellular kinase domains into close proximity, enabling mutual trans-autophosphorylation of specific Tyrosine residues on the activation loop and C-terminal tail.
csir_high_yield: Insulin Receptor Structural Exception: Unlike most RTKs that exist as monomers and dimerize upon ligand binding, the Insulin Receptor (InsR) is a pre-formed disulfide-linked heterotetramer (\alpha_2\beta_2) that undergoes a conformational rearrangement upon insulin binding.

Autophosphorylation serves two distinct roles: (1) relieving steric autoinhibition of the kinase domain; (2) creating high-affinity docking sites for intracellular signaling proteins containing SH2 or PTB domains.
pathology: HER2/ErbB2 Amplification in Breast Cancer: Overexpression or gene amplification of the HER2 receptor tyrosine kinase drives uncontrolled cellular division in ~20-25% of human breast cancers (treated with Trastuzumab/Herceptin).
lab_workbench: Phosphotyrosine Immunoprecipitation followed by Western Blotting with Anti-Phosphotyrosine antibodies (e.g., 4G10) to monitor acute growth factor-stimulated RTK activation.

node_cytokine_receptor.title: Class I & II Cytokine Receptors (JAK-STAT Activators)
node_cytokine_receptor.subtitle: Receptors Lacking Intrinsic Enzymatic Activity Associated with Non-Covalent Janus Kinases

metrics.structural_hallmark: Contain conserved extracellular cytokine receptor homology modules (WSXWS motif, fibronectin type III domains)
metrics.enzymatic_status: LACK intrinsic kinase activity; rely entirely on non-covalently bound JAK kinases (Jak1, Jak2, Tyk2)
metrics.ligand_examples: Interleukins (IL-2, IL-6), Interferons (IFN-\alpha/\gamma), Erythropoietin (EPO), Growth Hormone (GH)

mechanism: Cytokine receptors do not possess catalytic domains. Instead, their intracellular membrane-proximal domains are tightly bound to cytosolic tyrosine kinases of the Janus Kinase (JAK) family.

Cytokine binding induces receptor dimerization, bringing associated JAKs together so they can trans-phosphorylate and activate each other, subsequently phosphorylating receptor tyrosine residues to recruit STAT transcription factors.
csir_high_yield: The JAK-STAT Axiom (CSIR Part B/C): Unlike RTKs which autophosphorylate their own kinase domains, Cytokine Receptors are phosphorylated by associated JAKs because the receptor itself is enzymatically dead!
Conserved Structural Motifs: Class I cytokine receptors contain a signature Trp-Ser-X-Trp-Ser (WSXWS) motif in the extracellular domain essential for proper folding and ligand binding.
pathology: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID-X1): Mutations in the common gamma chain (\gamma_c, CD132) shared by receptors for IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, and IL-21 abolish T and NK cell development.
lab_workbench: Electrophoretic Mobility Shift Assay (EMSA / Gel Shift Assay): Detects sequence-specific nuclear binding of activated STAT dimers to radiolabeled gamma-activated site (GAS) DNA probes.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1I1R — Growth Hormone Receptor Complex with JAK2 Binding Architecture)
OMIM Database (JAK3 Deficiency in SCID)

metrics.lipid_composition: High concentration of Glycosphingolipids, Cholesterol, and Saturated Fatty Acids
metrics.physical_state: Liquid-ordered (l_o) phase floating within the more fluid liquid-unordered (l_d) phosphoglyceride bilayer

mechanism: Lipid rafts are dynamic, sub-micron nanoscale assemblies enriched in cholesterol and sphingolipids that compartmentalize cellular processes by concentrating specific signaling molecules (e.g., GPCRs, eNOS, Src kinases, GPI-anchored proteins).
Caveolae are flask-shaped invaginations of the plasma membrane stabilized by oligomeric Caveolin coat proteins that function in endocytosis, mechanotransduction, and localized signal transduction.
csir_high_yield: Classic Biochemical Isolation (CSIR Part C Experimental Question): Lipid rafts are operationally defined as 'Triton X-100 Insoluble Low-Density Fractions' (DRMs — Detergent-Resistant Membranes). Because sphingolipids and cholesterol resist cold non-ionic detergents, lipid rafts float to the top of sucrose density ultracentrifugation gradients!

Cholesterol Depletion: Treating cells with Methyl-beta-cyclodextrin (\mathrm{M}\beta\mathrm{CD}) extracts membrane cholesterol, disassembling lipid rafts and disrupting receptor tyrosine kinase signaling.
pathology: Congenital Generalized Lipodystrophy: Mutations in CAVIN1 or Caveolin-3 disrupt caveolae formation, leading to severe muscle wasting, cardiomyopathy, and metabolic dysfunction.
lab_workbench: Sucrose Density Gradient Ultracentrifugation: Cell lysates extracted in 1% Triton X-100 at 4°C are fractionated; lipid raft proteins segregate cleanly into low-density fractions (Fractions 2–4).

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (6H30 — Caveolin-1 Membrane Scaffolding Complex)

node_g_protein_cycle.title: Heterotrimeric G-Protein Activation Cycle
node_g_protein_cycle.subtitle: GTPase Switch: Gα Subunit Dissociation, GDP/GTP Exchange & Intrinsic GTPase Activity

metrics.subunit_composition: Heterotrimer of Alpha (\alpha), Beta (\beta), and Gamma (\gamma) subunits
metrics.switch_mechanism: GDP-bound (Inactive trimer) \rightarrow GEF action \rightarrow GTP-bound (\alpha and \beta\gamma effectors)
metrics.alpha_families: G_{s} (Stimulates AC), G_{i/o} (Inhibits AC), G_{q/11} (Activates PLC\beta), G_{12/13} (RhoGEF pathway)

mechanism: INACTIVE STATE: In the resting basal state, the G\alpha subunit binds GDP and forms a tight heterotrimer with the tightly prenylated G\beta\gamma dimer.
ACTIVATION: When an agonist binds the GPCR, the receptor acts as a Guanine nucleotide Exchange Factor (GEF), inducing G\alpha$ to release GDP and bind intracellular GTP.

EFFECTOR ENGAGEMENT: GTP binding causes G\alpha-GTP to undergo a conformational shift, dissociating from the receptor and from the G\beta\gamma dimer. Both G\alpha-GTP and free G\beta\gamma independently regulate downstream effector enzymes (like Adenylyl Cyclase or Phospholipase C).
TERMINATION: Gaseous intrinsic GTPase activity (accelerated by RGS proteins — Regulators of G-protein Signaling) hydrolyzes GTP back to GDP, causing G\alpha-GDP to reassociate with G\beta\gamma$.
csir_high_yield: G-Protein Subfamily Specificity (Must Memorize for CSIR Exams):
• G_s (Stimulatory): Activates Adenylyl Cyclase \rightarrow increases cAMP \rightarrow activates PKA.
• G_i (Inhibitory): Inhibits Adenylyl Cyclase \rightarrow decreases cAMP.
• G_q (Q-Pathway): Activates Phospholipase C beta (PLC\beta) \rightarrow cleaves \mathrm{PIP}_2 into \mathrm{IP}_3 + DAG \rightarrow mobilizes \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} and activates PKC.

Cholera Toxin vs. Pertussis Toxin (Classic CSIR Part C Question): Cholera toxin ADP-ribosylates Gs\alpha, locking it in the active GTP-bound state (continual cAMP surge); Pertussis toxin ADP-ribosylates Gi\alpha, locking it in the inactive GDP-bound state (preventing inhibition of AC).
pathology: McCune-Albright Syndrome: Activating somatic mosaic mutations in GNAS (encoding Gs\alpha) cause hormone hypersecretion, café-au-lait skin spots, and fibrous dysplasia of bone.
lab_workbench: \mathrm{[}^{35}\mathrm{S]\mathrm{GTP}\gamma\mathrm{S} Binding Assay: Measures GPCR agonist efficacy by quantifying the incorporation of non-hydrolyzable radiolabeled GTP into membrane-bound G-protein alpha subunits.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1AZT — Heterotrimeric G Protein Alpha-Beta-Gamma Complex)
OMIM Database (GNAS Mutations in Pseudohypoparathyroidism & McCune-Albright)

node_camp_pka_axis.title: Adenylyl Cyclase, cAMP & Protein Kinase A (PKA)
node_camp_pka_axis.subtitle: Cyclic AMP Second Messenger Synthesis & Tetrameric PKA Regulatory/Catalytic Dissociation

metrics.generator_enzyme: Adenylyl Cyclase (Integral membrane enzyme with 2 cytosolic catalytic domains)
metrics.pka_holoenzyme: Inactive Tetramer: 2 Regulatory (R) subunits + 2 Catalytic (C) subunits

mechanism: Active Gs\alpha-GTP binds and stimulates Adenylyl Cyclase (AC), converting cytosolic ATP into cyclic AMP (cAMP).

cAMP acts as a diffusible second messenger binding to the regulatory (R) subunits of Protein Kinase A (PKA). Binding of 4 cAMP molecules (2 per R subunit) induces a conformational change that releases the active catalytic (C) subunits.
Free catalytic PKA subunits translocate into the nucleus or phosphorylate cytoplasmic target enzymes (e.g., phosphorylase kinase and glycogen synthase to regulate glycogen metabolism).
csir_high_yield: Nuclear Transcription via PKA & CREB (CSIR Molecular Biology Core): Active PKA catalytic subunits enter the nucleus and phosphorylate CREB (cAMP Response Element-Binding Protein) at Serine-133. Phosphorylated CREB recruits the coactivator CBP/p300 (via its KIX domain), initiating transcription of cAMP-responsive genes containing CRE sequences (5'-TGACGTCA-3').
Phosphodiesterase (PDE) Regulation: Caffeine and Theophylline act as non-selective competitive inhibitors of cAMP Phosphodiesterase, elevating intracellular cAMP levels and prolonging PKA activity.
pathology: Carney Complex: Inactivating mutations in the PRKAR1A gene (encoding the regulatory R1\alpha subunit of PKA) lead to constitutive PKA activity, causing endocrine tumors, myxomas, and skin pigmentation anomalies.
lab_workbench: FRET-based cAMP Biosensor Imaging (Epac-based sensors): Live-cell fluorescence microscopy tracking real-time intracellular cAMP fluctuations upon GPCR agonist stimulation.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1CMK — Protein Kinase A Catalytic Subunit Crystal Structure)
OMIM Database (PRKAR1A Mutations in Carney Complex)

node_plc_ip3_dag.title: Phospholipase C (\text{PLC}\beta / \text{PLC}\gamma), \text{IP}_3$, DAG & PKC Activation
node_plc_ip3_dag.subtitle: Membrane Phospholipid Cleavage into Dual Second Messengers

metrics.ip3_receptor: Ligand-gated \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} release channel on the Smooth ER membrane
metrics.pkc_cofactors: Requires DAG + \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} + Phosphatidylserine for full enzymatic activation (Conventional PKC isoforms)

mechanism: The Gq-coupled GPCR pathway activates Phospholipase C-beta (\mathrm{PLC}\beta) — or RTKs activate \mathrm{PLC}\gamma via SH2 domain recruitment — which hydrolyzes membrane-bound \mathrm{PIP}_2 into two distinct second messengers:

1. \mathbf{IP_3} (Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate): Diffuses rapidly through the cytosol to bind \mathrm{IP}_3 Receptor (\mathrm{IP}_3\mathrm{R}) calcium channels on the ER membrane, triggering a massive efflux of stored \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} into the cytosol.
2. DAG (Diacylglycerol): Remains trapped within the plane of the plasma membrane where it recruits and activates Protein Kinase C (PKC) alongside the freshly released cytosolic \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} ions.
csir_high_yield: Dual Activation Requirement for PKC (CSIR Part C Staple): Conventional Protein Kinase C isoforms (\alpha, \beta\mathrm{I}, \beta\mathrm{II}, \gamma) require BOTH DAG (recruiting PKC to the membrane) AND \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} (inducing a conformational switch that ejects the autoinhibitory pseudosubstrate loop) to achieve full catalytic activity!

Lithium Chloride (\mathrm{LiCl}) Therapeutic Action: Inhibits Inositol Monophosphatase (IMPase), blocking the recycling of \mathrm{IP}_3$ breakdown products back into free inositol, depleting cellular \mathrm{PIP}_2$ pools (basis for treating bipolar disorder).
pathology: Angiomatosis & Sturge-Weber Syndrome: Somatic activating mutations in GNAQ (encoding Gq\alpha) hyperactivate the PLC pathway, driving unchecked vascular endothelial proliferation.
lab_workbench: Calcium Imaging with Fluo-4 AM or Fura-2: Confocal live-cell fluorescence microscopy capturing calcium spikes and oscillatory waves following \mathrm{IP}_3$ generation.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (2IDI — Phospholipase C Catalytic Domain Architecture)

node_calcium_calmodulin.title: Calcium (\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}) Signaling & Calmodulin (CaM)
node_calcium_calmodulin.subtitle: Ubiquitous EF-Hand Buffering & Calmodulin-Dependent Kinase (CaMKII) Activation

metrics.resting_cytosolic_ca: ~100 nM (Extracellular and ER lumen \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} are ~1–2 mM)
metrics.calmodulin_structure: Small 148-amino-acid acidic protein containing four EF-hand calcium-binding motifs
metrics.camkii_function: Molecular memory switch via autophosphorylation at Thr-286

mechanism: Cytosolic \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} concentrations are maintained at a steep ~10,000-fold gradient across membranes by active pumps (SERCA in ER, PMCA at plasma membrane, NCX sodium-calcium exchanger).

When \mathrm{IP}_3$ opens ER calcium stores, \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} binds cooperatively to **Calmodulin** (CaM). The \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}/CaM complex wraps around target enzymes like Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK), Calcineurin, and CaMKII, exposing their catalytic clefts.

CaMKII Activation & Memory: Binding of \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}/CaM exposes the CaMKII catalytic domain. Autophosphorylation of Threonine-286 locks CaMKII in an active state that persists even after \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} levels drop back to baseline (acting as a molecular memory switch in neurons).
csir_high_yield: The EF-Hand Motif (Classic CSIR Part B Structural Question): The EF-hand is a helix-loop-helix structural domain (found in Calmodulin, Troponin C, and Parvalbumin) where oxygen atoms from amino acid side chains coordinate an octahedral calcium ion.

Calcineurin & Immunosuppression: Calcineurin is a \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}/CaM-activated protein phosphatase that dephosphorylates NFAT (Nuclear Factor of Activated T cells), allowing NFAT to enter the nucleus and drive IL-2 transcription. Blocked by Cyclosporin A and Tacrolimus (FK506).
pathology: Darier-White Disease & Hailey-Hailey Disease: Caused by mutations in ER calcium pump genes (ATP2A2 or ATP2C1), disrupting epidermal calcium homeostasis and intercellular adhesion.
lab_workbench: BAPTA-AM Chelation Assay: Membrane-permeable intracellular calcium chelators trap cytosolic \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}, proving whether a downstream signaling event is calcium-dependent.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1CLL — Calcium-Calmodulin Complex Structure)

node_rtk_sh2_docking.title: RTK Trans-Autophosphorylation & SH2/PTB Domain Docking
node_rtk_sh2_docking.subtitle: Phosphotyrosine Recognition Modules & Adapter Assembly (Grb2 / SOS)

metrics.sh2_domain: Src Homology 2 domain (~100 amino acids; binds specific phosphotyrosine + 3-5 C-terminal residues)
metrics.adapter_example: Grb2 (Contains 1 SH2 domain flanked by 2 SH3 domains)

mechanism: Following RTK dimerization and trans-autophosphorylation, specific cytosolic proteins are recruited to the intracellular tail of the receptor through modular protein-interaction domains:
• **SH2 Domains**: Bind specifically to phosphorylated Tyrosine residues embedded in distinct amino acid contexts.
• **PTB Domains**: Bind Phosphotyrosine within Asn-Pro-X-Tyr (NPXY) motifs.

Example: The adapter protein **Grb2** uses its SH2 domain to bind phosphotyrosine on an activated EGFR, while its two SH3 domains bind proline-rich sequences on the nucleotide exchange factor **SOS** (Son of Sevenless), bringing SOS to the plasma membrane.
csir_high_yield: SH2 vs. SH3 Domain Specificity (Guaranteed CSIR Match-the-Following):
• SH2 Domains = Recognize and bind Phosphorylated Tyrosines (pTyr).
• SH3 Domains = Recognize and bind Proline-Rich Motifs (specifically PxxP consensus sequences).
• PH (Pleckstrin Homology) Domains = Bind membrane phosphoinositides (\mathrm{PIP}_2 / \mathrm{PIP}_3$).
pathology: Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia (CML) & the BCR-ABL Fusion Protein: The Philadelphia chromosome translocation t(9;22) fuses BCR to ABL1. The constitutively active BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase has aberrant SH2 domain interactions that drive unregulated proliferation of myeloid progenitor cells (treated with Imatinib/Gleevec).
lab_workbench: GST-Pull-Down Assay: Recombinant GST-tagged SH2 domains are used as bait to isolate specific phosphotyrosylated RTK complexes from cell lysates.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1SGB — Grb2 SH2 Domain Bound to Phosphotyrosine Peptide)
OMIM Database (BCR-ABL Fusion & CML Genetics)

node_ras_raf_mapk.title: The Ras–Raf–MEK–MAPK (ERK) Signaling Cascade
node_ras_raf_mapk.subtitle: Small GTPase Switch, Three-Tiered Kinase Module & Nuclear Gene Expression

metrics.small_gtpase: Ras (H-Ras, K-Ras, N-Ras) — Monomeric GTPase anchored via C-terminal farnesylation
metrics.mapkkk_tier1: Raf (MAPKKK) — Serine/Threonine kinase phosphorylated by Ras-GTP
metrics.mapkk_tier2: MEK1/2 (MAPKK) — Dual-specificity kinase phosphorylating Thr & Tyr on ERK
metrics.mapk_tier3: ERK1/2 (MAPK) — Translocates to nucleus to phosphorylate Elk-1, c-Fos, c-Jun

mechanism: STEP 1 (Ras Activation): Membrane-recruited SOS (GEF) converts inactive Ras-GDP into active **Ras-GTP**.
STEP 2 (Three-Tiered Kinase Cascade):
• **Tier 1 (MAPKKK)**: Ras-GTP recruits and activates **Raf**, which phosphorylates MEK.
• **Tier 2 (MAPKK)**: **MEK** (a dual-specificity kinase) phosphorylates both Threonine and Tyrosine residues on **ERK**.

• **Tier 3 (MAPK)**: Activated **ERK** homodimerizes and translocates into the nucleus, where it phosphorylates transcription factors (like Elk-1 and c-Fos) to drive cell cycle entry (Cyclin D expression).
csir_high_yield: Oncogenic Ras Mutations (Classic CSIR Part C Question): Mutations at Glycine-12 (G12D/V) or Glutamine-61 (Q61L) lock Ras in the active GTP-bound state because they sterically block the GTPase-activating protein (GAP) from stimulating intrinsic GTP hydrolysis, causing constitutive mitogenic signaling found in ~30% of all human cancers.
Dual-Specificity of MEK: MEK is unique because it phosphorylates BOTH Threonine and Tyrosine residues on the activation loop (T-E-Y motif) of ERK.
pathology: Noonan Syndrome: Germline activating mutations in PTPN11, SOS1, or RAF1 hyperactivate the Ras-MAPK pathway, causing facial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects, and short stature.
lab_workbench: Active-ERK Phospho-Specific Western Blotting (Anti-p44/42 MAPK): Quantifies rapid phosphorylation kinetics of ERK1/2 following mitogenic stimulation.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (4Q21 — Ras-GTP Complexed with Effector Raf Kinase Domain)
OMIM Database (KRAS Oncogene Mutations in Cancer)

node_jak_stat_cascade.title: The JAK–STAT Transcriptional Signaling Pathway
node_jak_stat_cascade.subtitle: Receptor Trans-Phosphorylation, STAT SH2 Dimerization & Nuclear Translocation

metrics.stat_proteins: STAT1 through STAT6 (Contain N-terminal DNA-binding domain + central SH2 domain + C-terminal transactivation domain)
metrics.nuclear_import: Mediated by Importin-alpha/beta following reciprocal SH2-phosphotyrosine dimerization

mechanism: STEP 1: Cytokine binding causes receptor dimerization, bringing associated JAKs together to trans-autophosphorylate each other and phosphorylate tyrosine residues on the receptor tail.
STEP 2: Cytosolic **STAT** (Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription) proteins dock onto these phosphotyrosines via their **SH2 domains**.
STEP 3: JAKs phosphorylate the docked STAT proteins on a conserved C-terminal Tyrosine residue.

STEP 4: Phosphorylated STATs dissociate from the receptor and form **reciprocal dimers** via intermolecular SH2-phosphotyrosine interactions. These active dimers translocate into the nucleus, bind specific promoter elements (GAS / ISRE), and activate transcription.
csir_high_yield: Reciprocal SH2 Dimerization (Classic CSIR Part C Staple): In a STAT dimer, the SH2 domain of STAT monomer A binds the phosphorylated tyrosine of STAT monomer B, AND the SH2 domain of monomer B binds the phosphorylated tyrosine of monomer A!

Negative Feedback via SOCS Proteins: Activated STATs induce transcription of **SOCS** (Suppressors of Cytokine Signaling) proteins, which bind JAKs or receptors and target them for proteasomal destruction, shutting off the pathway.
pathology: Polycythemia Vera: A somatic gain-of-function mutation in JAK2 (V617F) renders hematopoietic progenitor cells hypersensitive to erythropoietin, driving uncontrolled red blood cell production independently of EPO.
lab_workbench: Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP-qPCR): Validates in vivo binding of STAT1/STAT3 dimers to target gene promoters (e.g., IRF1 or SOCS1) following interferon stimulation.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1BF5 — STAT1 Homodimer Bound to DNA Target Sequence)
OMIM Database (JAK2 V617F Mutation in Myeloproliferative Neoplasms)

node_grk_arrestin.title: GPCR Desensitization: GRKs, Beta-Arrestin & Internalization
node_grk_arrestin.subtitle: Homologous Desensitization, Clathrin-Coated Pit Endocytosis & Arrestin Biasing

metrics.adapter_protein: Beta-Arrestin 1 & 2 (Stops G-protein coupling and targets receptor to clathrin pits)
metrics.fate_options: Lysosomal degradation vs. Endosomal dephosphorylation and recycling back to plasma membrane

mechanism: To prevent overstimulation, active GPCRs undergo rapid **homologous desensitization**:
1. **Phosphorylation**: G Protein-Coupled Receptor Kinases (GRKs) phosphorylate multiple Serine/Threonine residues on the cytosolic C-terminus and intracellular loops of the active GPCR.
2. **Arrestin Recruitment**: **Beta-Arrestin** binds these phosphorylated residues, sterically blocking further G-protein binding and effectively uncoupling the receptor.

3. **Internalization**: Beta-arrestin acts as an adapter, recruiting AP-2 and Clathrin to pull the receptor into clathrin-coated pits for endocytosis, where it is either degraded in lysosomes or recycled.
csir_high_yield: Arrestin-Mediated Signaling (Modern Paradigm): Beta-arrestin is not just a desensitization shutdown switch—it actively scaffolds its own independent signaling cascades (such as the Src and ERK MAPK pathways) independently of heterotrimeric G proteins ('Biased Agonism').
Heterologous Desensitization: PKA or PKC phosphorylates GPCRs at sites distinct from GRKs, dampening receptor responsiveness across un-stimulated pathways.
pathology: Impaired Beta-Arrestin trafficking contributes to heart failure progression, where chronic beta-adrenergic receptor hyperstimulation causes maladaptive receptor downregulation.
lab_workbench: Beta-Arrestin Translocation Assay (Bioluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer / BRET): Tracks real-time recruitment of GFP-tagged beta-arrestin to luciferase-tagged GPCRs upon agonist addition.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (4ZWJ — Beta-Arrestin Bound to Phosphorylated GPCR)

node_signaling_crosstalk.title: Signaling Crosstalk & Pharmacological Therapeutics
node_signaling_crosstalk.subtitle: Network Integration, Pathway Cross-Activation & Targeted Kinase Inhibitors

metrics.crosstalk_mechanism: Shared second messengers (\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}, cAMP) and multi-protein scaffolding complexes (AKAPs, KSR)
metrics.therapeutic_rtk_inhibitors: Small-molecule ATP-competitive kinase inhibitors (Imatinib, Gefitinib, Erlotinib)

mechanism: Intracellular signaling networks do not operate as isolated linear buckets; instead, they form richly integrated webs connected by signaling **crosstalk**.

For example, cAMP-activated PKA can cross-activate or inhibit the Raf-MAPK pathway depending on cell type by phosphorylating specific isoforms of Raf, while intracellular calcium waves integrate inputs from both GPCRs and RTKs.

Pharmacological targeting exploits these networks: small-molecule ATP-competitive inhibitors lock kinase domains in inactive conformations, while biological monoclonal antibodies block extracellular ligand binding.
csir_high_yield: AKAPs (A-Kinase Anchoring Proteins): Scaffolding proteins that tether PKA alongside other signaling enzymes (like Phosphodiesterases and Protein Phosphatases) right next to their specific intracellular targets, ensuring localized signal compartmentalization.

Type I vs. Type II Kinase Inhibitors: Type I inhibitors (e.g., Gefitinib) bind the active conformation of the kinase hinge region; Type II inhibitors (e.g., Imatinib) bind the inactive 'DFG-out' conformation.
pathology: Drug Resistance in Cancer: Secondary gatekeeper mutations (e.g., T315I mutation in BCR-ABL or T790M in EGFR) sterically block small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors from binding, causing clinical relapse.
lab_workbench: Reverse-Phase Protein Arrays (RPPA): High-throughput antibody-based profiling quantifying activation states of dozens of signaling nodes simultaneously across drug treatment timecourses.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (2BZ6 — EGFR Kinase Domain Bound to Gefitinib Inhibitor)
OMIM Database (Pharmacogenetics & Kinase Inhibitor Resistance)

agents.name: Cholera Toxin (Ctx)
agents.mechanism_of_action: ADP-ribosylates Arginine-201 of Gs\alpha, inhibiting intrinsic GTPase activity
agents.rescue_experiment: Classic CSIR NET Toxin Paradigm: Locks Gs\alpha in the active GTP-bound state, causing unremitting Adenylyl Cyclase activation, massive cAMP accumulation, and lethal chloride/water efflux in intestinal epithelial cells (severe secretory diarrhea).

agents.name: Pertussis Toxin (Ptx)
agents.mechanism_of_action: ADP-ribosylates Cysteine-352 on the C-terminus of Gi\alpha, preventing GPCR interaction
agents.rescue_experiment: Prevents Gi\alpha from coupling to GPCRs, locking Gi in the inactive GDP-bound state and abolishing inhibitory control over Adenylyl Cyclase (elevating basal cAMP).

agents.name: Imatinib (Gleevec)
agents.mechanism_of_action: Inactive 'DFG-out' conformation ATP-binding pocket of BCR-ABL, c-KIT, and PDGFR
agents.rescue_experiment: Miracle cancer therapeutic that specifically blocks BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase autophosphorylation in Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia, shutting down downstream MAPK and STAT survival signaling.

agents.name: Wortmannin / LY294002
agents.mechanism_of_action: ATP-binding catalytic cleft of PI3K (Blocks \mathrm{PIP}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{PIP}_3$ conversion)
agents.rescue_experiment: Halts production of \mathrm{PIP}_3$, preventing membrane recruitment of Akt/PKB and abolishing survival/anti-apoptotic signaling, leading to cell cycle arrest or apoptosis.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the heterotrimeric G-protein activation node whose Arginine residue is ADP-ribosylated by Cholera toxin, locking it in an active GTP state.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! Cholera toxin ADP-ribosylates Gs\alpha, preventing intrinsic GTPase activity and causing constitutive cAMP overproduction.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the Level 3 docking hub where Src Homology 2 (SH2) domains specifically recognize and bind phosphorylated Tyrosine residues.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Spot on! SH2 domains recognize pTyr residues on activated RTKs to nucleate downstream adapter complexes like Grb2-SOS.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the transcription factor activation cascade where monomers undergo reciprocal SH2-phosphotyrosine intermolecular dimerization before nuclear translocation.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Exact match! STAT proteins use their SH2 domains to bind reciprocal phosphotyrosines on partner monomers, forming active dimers for nuclear import.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the second messenger generation node that produces both water-soluble \mathrm{IP}_3$ and membrane-bound DAG to co-activate Protein Kinase C.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! Phospholipase C cleaves \mathrm{PIP}_2 into \mathrm{IP}_3$ (releasing ER calcium) and DAG (recruiting PKC to the membrane).
